title: Percentage not normalised in apply_discount() (app/pricing.py:23)
executive_summary: Run 20261107-203927-failure FAILED: 'Unit tests' failed (4 failed, 17 passed). Root cause (95% confidence): Percentage not normalised in apply_discount() (app/pricing.py:23). Production impact: None. The pipeline stopped at unit tests; no artifact was built or deployed. A minimal fix is proposed and awaits human approval.
root_cause: The latest commit changed app/pricing.py:23 in apply_discount() to multiply by 'discount_pct' directly. 'discount_pct' is on a 0-100 scale, so a 10% discount is applied as 1000%. Every failing assertion is consistent with this: observed discounts are exactly 100x the expected value, and totals go negative.

test_ten_percent_discount_amount: actual value is exactly 100x expected
test_discount_then_tax: actual value is exactly 100x expected
order totals go negative in test_ten_percent_discount_total
'discount_pct' (0-100 scale) used as a raw multiplier in apply_discount()

evidence.excerpt:

+    return to_money(subtotal * discount_pct)

evidence.finding: every failing test module imports app.pricing (directly or transitively)

impact.customer_impact: Any discounted order would be mispriced (discount 100x too large, negative totals) - direct revenue and trust impact if released.
impact.production_impact: None. The pipeline stopped at unit tests; no artifact was built or deployed.

recommendation: Restore percentage normalisation: change 'discount_pct' to '(discount_pct / HUNDRED)' on app/pricing.py:23. One-line change, no behaviour change for 0% discounts.
fix_guide: Re-run lint and the unit test stage (targeted validation).
Re-run the full pipeline to rebuild the artifact and run integration tests.
Add the 100x-ratio assertion pattern to code review guidance for money/percentage code.
alternatives_considered: Change tests to match new behaviour - rejected: tests encode the pricing contract; bot may not edit tests.
Revert the whole commit - viable, but broader than the one-line defect.
